Portuguese

[edit]
Portuguese Wikipedia has an article on:
jacaré
Wikipedia pt

Etymology

[edit]

    Borrowed from Old Tupi îakaré, from Proto-Tupi-Guarani *jakare.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ʒa.kaˈɾɛ/
    • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ʒɐ.kɐˈɾɛ/

    • Rhymes: -ɛ
    • Hyphenation: ja‧ca‧ré

    Noun

    [edit]

    jacaré m (plural jacarés, feminine (informal) jacaroa, feminine plural (informal) jacaroas)(chiefly Brazil)

    1. any crocodilian of the family Alligatoridae
    2. (strictly) caiman (any crocodilian of the subfamily Caimaninae)
      Synonym: caimão

    Usage notes

    [edit]

    The gender of this Portuguese zoonym is always masculine: when the gender of the being itself must be specified, jacaré-macho for male and jacaré-fêmea for female. Here, fêmea is treated as an undeclinable noun and doesn't necessarily need to agree in gender with the referent, but would change to fêmeo if so.
